corrections.how: Install the App Store app and pair with a setup code from the Control UI (Devices, Pair device) or openclaw qr. This gateway owns its Tailscale Serve route, so the code can carry the secure address. An administrator-minted setup code approves the device and the first command surface the app declares in one step, so read the approved command list afterwards with nodes describe; a separate pending approval appears only when the phone later widens its surface (camera, Health and so on). Gateway ceiling for iOS by default: camera.list, location.get, device.info, device.status, contacts.search, calendar.events, reminders.list, photos.latest, motion.activity, motion.pedometer, system.notify, plus talk.ptt.* for a Talk-capable node. Opt-in only through gateway.nodes.commands.allow: camera.snap, camera.clip, screen.record, health.summary, contacts.add, calendar.add, reminders.add. For agent access, prefer small in-house plugin tools that call api.runtime.nodes.invoke with the node id and command fixed in code. The built-in nodes tool is a poor grant: it is owner-only (dropped from any turn whose sender is not the command owner, which today is Tony alone), it is on the sandbox default deny list (so it needs tools.alsoAllow plus tools.sandbox.tools.alsoAllow), and it also carries approve, reject and raw invoke actions. If it is granted anyway, the before_tool_call hook must pin action, node id and command. Idle on a charger: the full surface answers only while the app is open in the foreground (keep-awake setting on, Guided Access holding the app on screen). Once the phone locks or the app is backgrounded, iOS may suspend the connection and the gateway gets only best-effort presence beacons and relay push wakes.
caveats: iOS has no notifications, SMS, call-log, installed-apps, mobile UI or computer-control commands; those exist only for Android or desktop nodes.
Camera and screen commands work only while the app is in the foreground.

Background is best-effort: Apple treats background pushes as low priority, tells senders not to exceed two or three an hour, does not guarantee delivery and allows 30 seconds of runtime; iOS decides when background refresh runs.

Pairing also gives the phone an operator session, and the iPhone app needs both node and operator credentials. The default code includes admin. The limited code only drops admin: in the installed code it still carries write, approvals, questions, read and talk-secrets scopes, and write scope lets the phone message any agent and relay commands to any paired node. The voice-node code is narrower (read and talk), but read covers session reads across the gateway.
The docs table is the gateway's ceiling, not proof of what the App Store build declares.

A paired node can itself post agent requests and voice transcripts to a session key the phone names, so a paired phone sits inside the gateway's single trust domain. OpenClaw says plainly that operator scopes are not isolation between people.

Named operator roles can limit a person to certain agents, but with roles configured the gateway rejects setup-code and device tokens for operator connections unless the connection carries a verified identity.
corrections.safety:
A paired phone adds sensors and personal data, and it is also a control surface: its operator token and its node events are not confined to one agent. Today only Tony's phone can be paired without weakening the rule that family members only chat; pairing Jordan's phone or a shared spare phone needs a decision on that rule first. Keep phone access off the research and mail-reader agents. Each

-main reaches only that person's phone through an in-house plugin tool with node id and commands fixed in code, not by prompt. Dangerous commands stay out of gateway.nodes.commands.allow until a specific feature needs one, and camera.clip, screen.record, contacts.add, calendar.add and reminders.add go into gateway.nodes.commands.deny.

corrections.how: As designed this does not stand on 2026.9.7. Pair the spare phone with a voice-node setup code: node credentials plus only operator.read and operator.talk. Under that token only Talk sessions are certain to be reachable (talk.client.*, talk.session.*, talk.speak need operator.talk). The native speech loop sends the transcript through Gateway chat, and chat.send is write-scoped, so expect to need realtime Talk, which on iOS means audio going to OpenAI with a Platform key or through the gateway relay. Set talk.agentId to a new shared 'kitchen' agent with no memory, no accounts and a short tool list (home_weather, add-to-list through the household store); that key owns Talk sessions created without an agent-prefixed session key. Voice Wake is a per-device switch that sends recognised commands to the session selected in the app. Keep the app on screen with keep-awake and Guided Access, with touch ignored so the session and agent pickers cannot be used. The app's Start Live Voice shortcut can start Talk by Siri.
caveats: iOS may suspend background audio, so the app has to stay open on screen. A HomePod or Siri handles timers and music more reliably.

The microphone cannot tell who is speaking, and the kids and guests will use it. Cloud speech and a cloud model for kids are on the never list, so this stays an adult convenience until a local model and local voice exist; the roadmap's kitchen speaker for the kids goes through Home Assistant for that reason.
Apple's speech recognition may use Apple's servers; realtime voice sends audio to OpenAI.
OpenClaw lists iOS realtime Talk on GPT-Live as not yet verified on a real device.
Wake words are one list for the whole gateway.

Wake-word routes to an agent exist in the data model, but this release exposes only voicewake.routing.get. I found no gateway method, CLI command or config key that writes a route, so per-phrase routing to a kitchen agent cannot be planned on.
talk.agentId is one gateway-wide setting, so it also becomes the default Talk owner for the parents' own phones.

With a voice-node token the realistic path is realtime voice, which sends everything the microphone hears, children included, to OpenAI. That collides with the rule against cloud speech for kids' content in a room the kids use.
corrections.safety: Because anyone in the room can speak to it, the kitchen agent must be safe for anyone: no private data, no memory, no web, no outbound messages. The voice-node credential cannot send chat messages or change settings, but it is not confined to the kitchen agent: operator.read covers session reads across the gateway, a Talk session can name any agent with an agent-prefixed session key, and the node can post voice transcripts to a session key it chooses. The only limits today are physical (Guided Access with touch ignored and a passcode) or adopting named operator roles. corrections.how: On the Android phone: Forward Notification Events on (off by default, needs Notification Listener access), Package Filter set to Allowlist with only the school and sports app ids, the per-minute cap left at 20, and Route Session Key pointing at a dedicated session. On the gateway: each forwarded notification is queued as a system event on the session key the phone sends, or on the system main session if none is set, with title and text cut to 120 characters each, and that session is woken. Point the key at a session of a reader agent with no tools and no memory. The reader's reply has no channel of its own, so an in-house plugin has to pick up its short structured output and send it to the pinned parents (the family delivery primitive, G009).
caveats: A notification carries a title and a short preview, and the gateway keeps at most 120 characters of each. No full post, no attachments.
Never use the default Blocklist mode: it forwards everything except the listed apps, including one-time codes and bank alerts.

The OpenClaw iPhone app has no notification commands. Shortcuts on iPhone has a Notification trigger, but Apple does not list it among automations that can run automatically, so an unattended relay from an iPhone is unconfirmed.
If the app offers email notifications, the school mailbox path (F051) is simpler and needs no extra phone.
If Route Session Key is left empty the events land in the system main session. Set it before turning forwarding on.
corrections.safety: Notification text is untrusted content, and the gateway delivers it as a system event rather than as wrapped untrusted input, so the receiving agent must have no tools and no memory and its output must be treated as untrusted too; delivery is done by code to pinned recipients. The session key is chosen on the phone, so anyone who can change that setting can aim notification text at another session: keep the phone physically secured. The package allowlist is the hard limit that keeps 2FA codes and financial alerts out. The phone holds no personal accounts beyond the school and team logins.
unverified: How to capture a tool-less reader's reply to a system-event wake and hand it to delivery code; I found no documented pattern for it.
How much text each app puts in its notifications.

Record these on the never list and enforce what can be enforced: keep sms.search and sms.send out of gateway.nodes.commands.allow and in gateway.nodes.commands.deny, and add notifications.list and notifications.actions to deny unless IPH-15 is built. Notification forwarding is a switch on the Android phone, not gateway config, so the rule there is allowlist mode only or off. Never install banking, brokerage, payment, wallet or email apps on a phone an agent can drive; never remove the passcode or disable auto-lock except inside Guided Access on a single harmless app; never register Happy's number or Apple Account as a recovery or second-factor channel for a parent's account.
